questions.question: In which type of farming, the land is used for growing food and fodder crops and rearing livestock?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mixed farming**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mixed farming** is a type of farming where the land is used for both **growing food and fodder crops as well as rearing livestock.**
 
• It involves a** combination of crop production and animal husbandry**.
 
• In **mixed farming systems, farmers grow crops such as wheat, maize, vegetables, fruits, etc., for food production, while also keeping livestock like cattle, sheep, goats, or poultry for meat, milk, eggs, and other by-products.**
 
• This type of farming allows farmers to have a diversified income stream and optimize the use of available resources by** integrating crop and animal production.**

​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dairy farming:**

 
 
• Dairy farming is a type of farming focused on the production of milk and milk products.
 
• It involves raising dairy animals, typically cows, but also goats or sheep, to obtain milk that can be processed into various products such as butter, cheese, yogurt, and ice cream. 
 
 
 
• **Plantation farming: **
 
 
• Plantation farming is a type of farming that involves the large-scale cultivation of a single crop, typically cash crops such as tea, coffee, rubber, sugarcane, palm oil, or bananas.
 
• It is commonly practiced in tropical or subtropical regions with favorable climate conditions for the specific crop. 
 
 
 
• **Commercial farming:**
 
 
• Commercial farming refers to agricultural practices that focus on producing crops or livestock for sale in the market, with the primary goal of generating profit.
 
• It typically involves large-scale production and the use of modern technologies, machinery, and inputs such as fertilizers and pesticides.

questions.question: Identify the crop which is grown in Kharif cropping season in Northern States of India.

__
 
• **Rice** is predominantly grown during the Kharif cropping season in Northern States of India.
 
• The Kharif cropping season typically starts with the onset of the monsoon in June and lasts until October.
 
• Rice requires a hot and humid climate with substantial rainfall, which aligns with the conditions during the Kharif season in Northern India.
 
• Other crops grown in the Kharif season include maize, sorghum, and pulses, but rice is the most significant among them.
 
• States such as Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, and Bihar are major producers of Kharif rice.

• Rice is a staple food for a large part of the Indian population, especially in the eastern and southern regions.
 
• The government provides various subsidies and support mechanisms to encourage rice cultivation during the Kharif season.
 
• Modern agricultural practices and irrigation facilities have further enhanced rice yield in these regions.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements about Green Revolution is/are correct?

I. India became self-reliant after the advent of the Green Revolution.

II. Due to the Green Revolution, the soil started losing nutrients due to repeated cultivation of the same crop.

III. Green revolution caused depletion of fresh ground water.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**i, ii and iii**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Green Revolution in India led to self-reliance in terms of food grain production, transforming the country from a food-deficient nation to one that could sustain itself.
 
• Repetitive cultivation of the same high-yield variety (HYV) crops led to soil nutrient depletion, as these crops absorbed specific nutrients in large quantities.
 
• The Green Revolution intensified the use of water resources for irrigation, leading to the depletion of fresh groundwater levels, especially in regions like Punjab and Haryana.
 
• The use of chemical fertilizers and pesticides increased significantly during the Green Revolution, contributing to environmental degradation and impacting soil health.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Green Revolution:**

 
 
• The Green Revolution refers to the period during the 1960s and 1970s when agriculture in many developing countries was transformed by the adoption of high-yielding variety (HYV) seeds, chemical fertilizers, and advanced irrigation techniques.
 
• It aimed to increase food production to combat hunger and improve food security.
 
• Countries like India and Mexico saw significant increases in crop production, particularly in wheat and rice.
 
• Despite its success in increasing food production, the Green Revolution also led to environmental issues, including soil degradation, water scarcity, and loss of biodiversity.
 
 
 
• **Soil Nutrient Depletion:**
 
 
• Continuous cultivation of the same crop without crop rotation can lead to the depletion of specific nutrients in the soil.
 
• This results in reduced soil fertility, necessitating the increased use of chemical fertilizers to maintain crop yields.
 
• Over time, this can lead to soil degradation and reduced agricultural sustainability.
 
 
 
• **Groundwater Depletion:**
 
 
• Intensive irrigation practices, particularly in regions with limited water resources, can lead to the over-extraction of groundwater.
 
• This can cause a decline in water tables, making it more difficult and expensive to access water for irrigation in the long term.
 
• Regions like Punjab and Haryana in India have experienced significant groundwater depletion due to the Green Revolution.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Impact:**
 
 
• The increased use of chemical fertilizers and pesticides associated with the Green Revolution has led to environmental pollution.
 
• These chemicals can contaminate soil and water bodies, adversely affecting plant and animal life.
 
• There are also health concerns for humans exposed to these chemicals through food and water.

This type of cultivation is often used to produce crops that are resistant to pests and diseases, have higher yields, and can tolerate harsh environmental conditions.

questions.question:
Read the following about the impact of Green Revolution to the farmers in India.

A. The introduction of the Green Revolution helped the farmers in raising their level of income.

B. Farmers ploughed back their surplus income for improving agricultural productivity.

Identify the INCORRECT statement/statements.

The correct answer is __**Neither A nor B**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** **Impact of Green Revolution on Farmers in India:**

__
 
• The **Green Revolution** was a period when agriculture in India was converted to an industrial system due to the adoption of modern methods and technology such as **high-yielding variety (HYV) seeds, tractors, irrigation facilities, pesticides, and fertilizers**.
 
• **Statement A:** The introduction of the Green Revolution helped the farmers in raising their level of income. This statement is correct. The Green Revolution led to an **increase in agricultural production**, which in turn increased the income levels of many farmers.
 
• **Statement B:** Farmers plowed back their surplus income to improve agricultural productivity. This statement is also correct. Many farmers **reinvested their increased income** into their farms to further enhance productivity by purchasing better seeds, fertilizers, and farming equipment.
 
• As both statements A and B are correct, the answer is **option 2) Neither A nor B**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Mechanization

• Boosted the agricultural economy and reduced dependency on food imports.
 
• This led to changes in the rural economy and lifestyle, including increased income for farmers.
 
 
 
• **Challenges:**

• Inequality: Benefits were not evenly distributed, with larger farmers gaining more than smaller ones.

questions.question: What was the pre-determined principle announced in the Union Budget for 2018-19 regarding the Minimum Support Price (MSP) for the principal crops in India?

options.text: Equal to the cost of production
One-and-a-half times the cost of production
50 per cent less than the cost of production

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**One-and-a-half times the cost of production**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In the Union Budget for 2018-19, the government announced that the Minimum Support Price (MSP) for all principal crops would be set at **one-and-a-half times (1.5x) the cost of production**.
 
• This decision aimed to ensure remunerative prices for farmers and address the issue of agrarian distress in the country.
 
• The MSP calculation is based on the comprehensive cost of production, including expenses such as seeds, fertilizers, labor, irrigation, and other inputs.
 
• The announcement was in line with the Swaminathan Commission's recommendations, which advocated fixing MSP at least 50% higher than the cost of production.
 
• The initiative was primarily targeted at improving farmers' income and boosting agricultural productivity in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Minimum Support Price (MSP):**

 
 
• MSP is a form of market intervention by the Government of India to safeguard farmers against sharp price falls during bumper production years.
 
• The MSP is announced for 22 mandated crops and is determined by the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA).
 
• It is based on the recommendations of the Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP).
 
 
 
• **Swaminathan Commission:**
 
 
• The National Commission on Farmers, chaired by Dr. M.S. Swaminathan, recommended fixing MSP at least 50% above the cost of production (C2).
 
• The formula includes both input costs (A2) and the imputed value of family labor (FL).
 
 
 
• **Types of Costs in MSP Calculation:**
 
 
• **A2:** Includes out-of-pocket expenses like seeds, fertilizers, and labor.
 
• **A2+FL:** A2 costs plus the imputed value of unpaid family labor.
 
• **C2:** Comprehensive cost, including A2+FL and the rental value of owned land and interest on fixed capital.
 
 
 
• **Implementation and Benefits:**
 
 
• The 1.5x MSP policy ensures better income for farmers and reduces their dependence on informal credit systems.
 
• It also incentivizes crop diversification and adoption of sustainable farming practices.
